lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Number eight is in Los Angeles. Call me BEFORE you touch it. I sharpened the pencil.
lines.script: [brisk, bossy] Number eight is in Los Angeles. [firm, urgent] Call me BEFORE you touch it. [proud, matter-of-fact] I sharpened the pencil.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I promise. I packed a ruler.
lines.script: [quiet, sincere] I promise. [dry, deadpan] I packed a RULER.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Welcome home. Don't open the salad spinner. That's loaf thirty-one.
lines.script: [mellow, warm] welcome home. [easy, matter-of-fact] don't open the salad spinner. [relaxed] that's loaf thirty-one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You started without me. I made a schedule on the plane. It has tabs.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Bready Mercury was climbing out of the crock at five this morning. I wasn't going to argue with him.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Forty loaves, two at a time, forty-five minutes each. That's fifteen hours of oven, and we have nine.
lines.script: [quick, calculating] Forty loaves, two at a time, forty-five minutes each. [rising, tense] That's fifteen HOURS of oven, [flat, grim] and we have nine.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: So we bring twenty-four and tell Bernadette it's a tasting menu.
lines.script: [mellow, easy] so we bring twenty-four and tell bernadette [punchline, deadpan] it's a tasting menu.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She'll count them. She counted the folding chairs at Mr. Washington's birthday.
lines.script: [wary, certain] She'll count them. [dry, remembering] She counted the folding chairs at Mr. Washington's birthday.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She came by at seven to check on us. She called me the Other Tom and said my bowls were too close together.
lines.script: [mellow, easy] she came by at seven to check on us. [amused, laid-back] she called me the other tom and said my bowls were too close together.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: What did you tell her?

lines.text: I said, 'Great note, Bernadette.' Then she stood there waiting for me to move them, and I opened a soda.
lines.script: [mellow, easy] i said, great note, bernadette. [lazy, amused] then she stood there waiting for me to move them, [unhurried, deadpan] and i opened a soda.

lines.text: How long did she wait?
lines.script: [delighted, leaning in] How long did she WAIT?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It was a long soda.
lines.script: [mellow, deadpan] it was a long soda.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I've seen this movie, you know. The lady who runs the potluck always has something in her basement.
lines.script: [mellow, knowing] i've seen this movie, you know. [easy, lightly ominous] the lady who runs the potluck always has something in her basement.

lines.text: She doesn't have a basement. She has that shed with the two padlocks.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Two padlocks. On a shed.

lines.text: Tom! Get out here and look at my roses!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's your whole rosebush. It's inside an orange block the size of a minivan.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: And the red's gone out of everything around it. The roses, the lawn, my good hose. All grey.
lines.script: [bitter, aggrieved] And the red's gone out of everything around it. [pained, listing] The roses, the lawn, my good HOSE. [flat, hurt] All grey.

lines.text: You're the one who's always on a plane, Tom. Did you bring this home with you?
lines.script: [suspicious, pointed] You're the one who's always on a plane, Tom. [narrowed, accusing] Did you bring this home with you?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No, sir. But I've seen seven of them, and I know how to open one.
lines.script: [respectful, firm] No, sir. [steady, reassuring] But I've seen SEVEN of them, and I know how to open one.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Seven. And it never once came up at a block meeting.
lines.script: [dry, stunned] Seven. [wounded, pedantic] And it never once came up at a block meeting.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'm going to stand over here, on the part of the sidewalk that still has a color.
lines.script: [mellow, polite] i'm going to stand over here, [calm, firm] on the part of the sidewalk that still has a color.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: They don't do anything. They just sit there.
lines.script: [reassuring, easy] They don't do anything. [patient] They just sit there.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That's what I don't like about it. The dough rises. The dog jumps. That thing is just waiting.
lines.script: [mellow, uneasy] that's what i don't like about it. [low, thoughtful] the dough rises. the dog jumps. [quiet, ominous] that thing is just waiting.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Washington, there's a notice taped to your roses in there.
lines.script: [noticing, careful] Mr. Washington, there's a notice taped to your roses in there.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: That'll be from her.
lines.script: [weary, certain] That'll be from HER.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: 3468. You're back. Don't touch that. It's on my street.
lines.script: [clipped, commanding] Three four six eight. You're back. [sharp] Don't touch that. [possessive, flat] It's on MY street.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: 8:42 this morning. White sedan, parked across the Washington driveway for four minutes. Rental. Airport lot sticker on the windshield. I have the plate.
lines.script: [crisp, reporting] Eight forty-two this morning. White sedan, parked across the Washington driveway for four minutes. [dry, precise] Rental. Airport lot sticker on the windshield. [satisfied, flat] I have the PLATE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You saw a person do this?
lines.script: [intent, quiet] You saw a PERSON do this?

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: One man. Long coat, in this heat. He pointed something at the roses, there was a flash, and when I could see again, there was that.
lines.script: [crisp, disapproving] One man. [dry] Long coat, in this heat. [measured, reporting] He pointed something at the roses, there was a flash, [flat, gesturing] and when I could see again, there was THAT.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Then something small and on fire picked a gold thing up off the sidewalk and ran toward the boulevard. I wrote it down as a raccoon. I know it wasn't a raccoon.
lines.script: [crisp, reporting] Then something small and on fire picked a gold thing up off the sidewalk and ran toward the boulevard. [dry, reluctant] I wrote it down as a raccoon. [flat, certain] I know it wasn't a raccoon.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Bernadette, that's the most useful thing anyone has told me in eight of these.
lines.script: [sincere, impressed] Bernadette, that's the most useful thing anyone has told me in EIGHT of these.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Write that down and sign it. Nobody on this street ever does.
lines.script: [brusque, pleased underneath] Write that down and sign it. [dry, grumbling] Nobody on this street ever does.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: He was here fifteen minutes before your cab, 3468. You'd have seen him yourself if you were ever home.
lines.script: [dry, pointed] He was here fifteen minutes before your cab, three four six eight. [flat, jabbing] You'd have seen him yourself if you were ever HOME.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: The only thing at the end of the boulevard is the old Car Barn. My father drove the night streetcar out of it.
lines.script: [thoughtful, gruff] The only thing at the end of the boulevard is the old Car Barn. [quieter, proud] My father drove the night streetcar out of it.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Chained since 1963. I have the key. Nobody has ever asked me for it.
lines.script: [flat, dry] Chained since nineteen sixty-three. [pointed, matter-of-fact] I have the key. [deadpan] Nobody has ever ASKED me for it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Before I touch anything, I have to make a phone call. I promised a nine-year-old.
lines.script: [firm, polite] Before I touch anything, I have to make a phone call. [dry, straightforward] I promised a nine-year-old.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Then she can run the block meeting, because she'd be the first person on this street to keep a promise.
lines.script: [dry, grudging] Then she can run the block meeting, [sharp, deadpan] because she'd be the first person on this street to keep a promise.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. Did you touch it?
lines.script: [sharp, intent] Tata. [serious, demanding] Did you TOUCH it?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I did not touch it. Look. Round hole, burnt bulb, grey patch.
lines.script: [calm, proud] I did NOT touch it. [steady, showing] Look. Round hole, burnt bulb, grey patch.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: How big?
lines.script: [sharp, businesslike] How BIG?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A minivan.
lines.script: [plain, awed] A minivan.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's bigger than the golf cart. And it's in Los Angeles. I said Los Angeles.
lines.script: [thrilled, precise] That's bigger than the golf cart. [rising, triumphant] And it's in Los Angeles. [proud, savoring] I said LOS ANGELES.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Is that the chart? It has a key. It's color coded. That's the wall the detective has right before they take his badge away.
lines.script: [mellow, impressed] is that the chart? it has a key. it's color coded. [easy, delighted] that's the wall the detective has right before they take his badge away.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Thank you. Who's the lady behind you with the clipboard?
lines.script: [pleased, polite] Thank you. [curious, direct] Who's the lady behind you with the clipboard?

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Who's asking?
lines.script: [sharp, suspicious] Who's asking?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm Grace. I'm nine. I keep the chart.
lines.script: [crisp, official] I'm Grace. I'm nine. [proud, matter-of-fact] I keep the CHART.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace, somebody saw a man do this one. He came in a rental car.
lines.script: [quick, careful] Grace, somebody saw a man do this one. [steady] He came in a rental car.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A person! I said it was a person. What kind of car? What time? Did anybody get the license plate?

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: White sedan. 8:42. Yes.
lines.script: [clipped, flat] White sedan. [crisp] Eight forty-two. [satisfied] Yes.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, I like her.
lines.script: [delighted, sincere] Tata, I like HER.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Give the niece my number, 3468. And don't get ideas. I'm not being friendly. She keeps records, and I respect records.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: There are two of them now.
lines.script: [mellow, quietly awed] there are two of them now.

lines.speaker: Tom

lines.script: [dry, resigned] I know. [deadpan] They're going to start a newsletter.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: BOO!
lines.script: [gleeful, shouting] BOO!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Why didn't he jump?

lines.text: I watch a lot of scary movies. That was good, though. Top ten.
lines.script: [mellow, fair] i watch a lot of scary movies. [easy, generous] that was good, though. [warm, deadpan] top ten.

lines.speaker: Rose

lines.text: The gold coin is with the biggest thing that woke up. Find it, put it in the hole, and call me when the color comes back.
lines.script: [brisk, instructing] The gold coin is with the biggest thing that woke up. [firm, businesslike] Find it, put it in the hole, [proud, final] and call me when the color comes back.

lines.text: It ran toward the boulevard, and it was on fire.

lines.text: That's new. I need a new color for fire.
lines.script: [thoughtful, intrigued] That's new. [scribbling, matter-of-fact] I need a new color for FIRE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Our pilot light just walked out of the house.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Through the dog door. Nara's never once used the dog door.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We have forty loaves of raw dough and no fire.
lines.script: [tense, level] We have forty loaves of raw dough and NO fire.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Then I guess we're following a flame down the street. Bring the dough. I'm not leaving loaf thirty-one alone with the dog.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's loaf thirty-one.
lines.script: [dignified, patient] It's loaf thirty-one.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: And this one is drinking purple soda before noon.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It's the only thing on this street that's the right temperature.
lines.script: [mellow, deadpan] it's the only thing on this street that's the right temperature.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Don't be smart, Other Tom.

lines.text: So we're not going in?
lines.script: [hopeful, careful] So we're not going in?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Oh, we're going in. I just want it on the record that I knew.
lines.script: [mellow, cheerful] oh, we're going in. [easy, wry] i just want it on the record that i knew.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Forty loaves. Six o'clock. I don't care what's in there.
lines.script: [clipped, final] Forty loaves. Six o'clock. [flat, unmoved] I don't care what's in there.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Tom. That's a turntable. They used to spin a whole streetcar on that.
lines.script: [mellow, hushed, thrilled] tom. that's a turntable. [reverent, quiet] they used to spin a whole streetcar on that.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Do you need a minute?
lines.script: [gentle, amused] Do you need a minute?

lines.speaker: TNB

lines.script: [mellow, dreamy] i need about an hour. [easy, generous] but go ahead.

lines.speaker: Damp Blanket
lines.text: First it's one little flame. Then it's music. Then people have friends over. I've seen where it goes.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We're having forty people over at six.

lines.speaker: Damp Blanket
lines.text: Then I got here just in time.
lines.script: [grim, smug] Then I got here just in TIME.

lines.speaker: Damp Blanket
lines.text: Fine. Have your fun. Keep it down after ten.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Did you feel that?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hi. We can hear you.

lines.speaker: The Draft
lines.text: It's an old building. They all do this. Have you tried a sweater?
lines.script: [slippery, landlord-like] It's an old building. They all do this. [breezy, unhelpful] Have you tried a sweater?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You're holding one of our flames.
lines.script: [firm, patient] You're holding one of our flames.

lines.text: I'm not holding anything. That flame was like that when I got here.
lines.script: [airy, defensive] I'm not holding anything. [smooth, shifting blame] That flame was like that when I got here.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You sound exactly like my first landlord.

lines.speaker: The Draft
lines.text: I'll be back in the winter. I always am.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The starter is nine years old and it has a name.

lines.speaker: TNB

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nara, this is what you sound like.

lines.speaker: Picky Lunchbox

lines.speaker: TNB

lines.speaker: Tom

lines.speaker: TNB

lines.script: [grudging, instructing] Better. [gruff, coaching] Cut the top deeper next time. [dry, matter-of-fact] It needs somewhere to go.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: Hm. That one's a loaf.
lines.ctx: chapter 8 (new, fight line, after loaf three)
lines.script: [low, grudging approval] Hm. [gruff, quiet] That one's a LOAF.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: That's the first bread out of me since 1963. Don't stand there looking at it. Cut it.
lines.script: [gruff, moved but hiding it] That's the first bread out of me since nineteen sixty-three. [brusque, covering] Don't stand there looking at it. [gruff] Cut it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: There's a gold coin on your door. I need it, and I have to tell you what it does before I take it.
lines.script: [respectful, careful] There's a gold coin on your door. [steady, honest] I need it, [serious] and I have to tell you what it does before I take it.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: I know what it is. It's my pension. Sixty years late, and a little flame carried it in this morning.
lines.script: [gruff, certain] I know what it is. [proud, flat] It's my PENSION. [gruff, vindicated] Sixty years late, and a little flame carried it in this morning.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It isn't your pension. It opens an orange block on our street. When it does, every flame goes home and you go back to being an oven. A cold one. You won't be able to talk.
lines.script: [gentle, honest] It isn't your pension. [steady] It opens an orange block on our street. [careful, plain] When it does, every flame goes home and you go back to being an oven. [quiet, sorry] A cold one. [soft] You won't be able to talk.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: So it's not even mine.
lines.script: [slow, flat] So it's not even MINE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No. It has a rosebush on it.
lines.script: [gentle, plain] No. [quiet, honest] It has a rosebush on it.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: Sixty years, and the first gold through that door belongs to a shrub.
lines.script: [disbelieving, dry, wounded pride] Sixty years, [flat, bitter] and the first gold through that door belongs to a SHRUB.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: What time is this potluck?
lines.script: [gruff, abrupt] What time is this potluck?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Six o'clock.
lines.script: [plain, careful] Six o'clock.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: How many loaves?
lines.script: [gruff, businesslike] How many loaves?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Forty.
lines.script: [mellow, easy] forty.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: I used to do two hundred before midnight. Load me. If this is my last shift, I'm not ending it on three.
lines.script: [gruff, proud, rousing] I used to do two hundred before midnight. [commanding] Load me. [firm, dignified] If this is my last shift, I'm not ending it on THREE.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: Somebody's going to stand up tonight and say they arranged this bread. Somebody always did.
lines.script: [dry, knowing] Somebody's going to stand up tonight and say they arranged this bread. [flat, weary] Somebody ALWAYS did.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We know exactly who.
lines.script: [mellow, deadpan] we know exactly who.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: Take your shrub money. And shut my door on the way out. I'd like to cool down slowly.
lines.script: [gruff, letting go] Take your shrub money. [low, tired] And shut my door on the way out. [quiet, dignified] I'd like to cool down slowly.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you for the bread.
lines.script: [quiet, sincere] Thank you for the bread.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It goes in the round hole. It's your rosebush, so it should be you.
lines.script: [warm, simple] It goes in the round hole. [steady, kind] It's your rosebush, so it should be YOU.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: If this turns out to be a parking meter, I'm going to be upset.
lines.script: [gruff, suspicious] If this turns out to be a parking meter, [dry, warning] I'm going to be upset.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: 'Trim to regulation height.' Bernadette, you taped a notice to my roses.
lines.script: [reading, flat] Trim to regulation height. [disbelieving, turning] Bernadette, you taped a notice to my ROSES.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: At 5:30 this morning. Before the incident. It still applies.
lines.script: [crisp, unbothered] At five thirty this morning. [firm] Before the incident. [flat, immovable] It still applies.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: It was inside a block all day.
lines.script: [dry, incredulous] It was inside a block all DAY.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: The date's on it.
lines.script: [flat, final] The date's on it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Now I'll stand on the lawn.
lines.script: [mellow, relieved] okay. [easy, content] now i'll stand on the lawn.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: That bulb is evidence, 3468.
lines.script: [sharp, possessive] That bulb is evidence, three four six eight.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's going in my mother's junk drawer with the other seven.
lines.script: [polite, firm] It's going in my mother's junk drawer with the other seven.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Then I want it logged first.
lines.script: [dry, immovable] Then I want it LOGGED first.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Thirty-eight. Thirty-nine. That's thirty-nine, 3468. I said forty.
lines.script: [counting, precise] Thirty-eight. Thirty-nine. [flat, accusing] That's thirty-nine, three four six eight. [sharp] I said FORTY.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: That's my dog under the table, and I've never seen that loaf before in my life.
lines.script: [quick, innocent, sharp] That's my dog under the table, [deadpan, sweet] and I've never seen that loaf before in my LIFE.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: The dog owes this street a loaf.
lines.script: [stern, flat] The dog owes this street a loaf.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: She can get in line. She owes me a couch.
lines.script: [dry, quick] She can get in line. [wry, deadpan] She owes me a COUCH.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: I've got it. Nobody get up.
lines.script: [calm, unbothered, under load] I've got it. [easy, gentle] Nobody get up.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: He's got it.
lines.script: [dry, fond, not looking] He's got it.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: Tom. A rosebush got sealed in orange glass, every stove on the block went out, and it was all fixed by six. I'd love a quote.
lines.script: [brisk, reporter] Tom. [rapid, delighted] A rosebush got sealed in orange glass, every stove on the block went out, and it was all fixed by six. [sweet, sharp] I'd love a QUOTE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No comment.
lines.script: [prim, deadpan] No comment.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: That's a quote. I'm using it.
lines.script: [gleeful, quick] That's a QUOTE. [pleased, final] I'm using it.

lines.speaker: Miss Odette
lines.text: Bernadette, your diagram had my gumbo behind the paper plates.
lines.script: [pointed, Creole warmth] Bernadette, your diagram had my gumbo behind the paper plates.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: Hot dishes on the left. Everyone got the diagram.
lines.script: [crisp, defensive] Hot dishes on the left. [flat, firm] Everyone got the DIAGRAM.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: Everyone got it. Then we moved the table.
lines.script: [dry, serene] Everyone got it. [calm, delighted] Then we moved the table.

lines.speaker: Bernadette
lines.text: If I could have your attention. The Watch would like to thank the Watch for arranging the bread.
lines.script: [formal, tapping a glass] If I could have your attention. [grand, flat] The Watch would like to thank the Watch for arranging the bread.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He called it.
lines.script: [mellow, quietly delighted] he called it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Somebody always did.
lines.script: [dry, low, delighted] Somebody always did.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Hold on. This is the Car Barn loaf. My father brought one home every morning until they shut that place. Who baked this?
lines.script: [slow, stopped short] Hold on. [quiet, wondering] This is the Car Barn loaf. [soft, remembering] My father brought one home every morning until they shut that place. [gruff, asking] Who baked this?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: An old-timer from the barn. He retired today.
lines.script: [gentle, plain] An old-timer from the barn. [quiet, warm] He retired today.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Well, he took his time about it. You know, in 1979, when I bought that house...
lines.script: [gruff, softening] Well, he took his time about it. [settling in, storyteller] You know, in nineteen seventy-nine, when I bought that house...

lines.speaker: The Neighbors
lines.text: Thirty-eight thousand dollars, and the porch was already crooked.
lines.ctx: chapter 8 (new, Olivia, Miss Odette, Doña Carmen and Bernadette together)
lines.script: [in unison, flat, bored, together] Thirty-eight thousand dollars, [deadpan, together] and the porch was already crooked.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: I'm glad somebody on this street listens.
lines.script: [dry, satisfied] I'm glad somebody on this street LISTENS.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The drawer is ready for number eight. Also, a fancy letter came for you from the Moon Club. That place has been locked since 1971. I did not open it.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, brisk] The drawer is ready for number eight. [warm Long Island accent, curious] Also, a fancy letter came for you from the Moon Club. [warm Long Island accent, firm] That place has been locked since nineteen seventy-one. [warm Long Island accent, proud] I did not OPEN it.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I held it up to the lamp. There's a piano on it.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, conspiratorial] I held it up to the lamp. [warm Long Island accent, intrigued] There's a PIANO on it.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Your father says he once baked sixty loaves in one morning. He has never baked.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, dry] Your father says he once baked sixty loaves in one morning. [warm Long Island accent, flat, deadpan] He has NEVER baked.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The man rented a car AT THE AIRPORT. That means he flies back and forth. Like you. The next one is here. Come home.
lines.script: [urgent, triumphant] The man rented a car AT THE AIRPORT. [sharp, working it out] That means he flies back and forth. [pointed] Like YOU. [serious, firm] The next one is here. [quiet, plain] Come home.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I have to fly back tomorrow.
lines.script: [quiet, plain] I have to fly back tomorrow.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I figured. Take a loaf for your mom.
lines.script: [mellow, easy] i figured. [warm] take a loaf for your mom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That leaves you alone on this street with Bernadette.
lines.script: [concerned, dry] That leaves you alone on this street with Bernadette.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We're fine. She thinks I moved the bowls.
lines.script: [mellow, content] we're fine. [easy, deadpan] she thinks i moved the bowls.
